newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India demands halt to U.S.-based callback services.
newsitem.headline: India demands halt to U.S.-based callback services.

text.p: India supports moves to reduce payouts made between telephone companies for international calls but wants to stop "illegal" callback services, Communications Minister Beni Prasad Verma said on Thursday.

"I realise that rates should be reduced, not only to India but to other countries as well, but America should stop callback to this country," Verma told a news conference at the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair.
"Callback is illegal in my country," he said.
Verma said a large portion of international calls were now done via callback -- which enables payment at the cheaper end of the call, invariably in the United States.

He said Washington had agreed to send a team to India for a bilateral meeting about the imbalance of payments after the United States said in December it would cut unilaterally the so-called accounting rates.
People usually pay their local telephone company for international calls. It pays the company in the recipient country for the completion of the call at the accounting rate.
Last year, the United States, which has the heaviest volume added to by callback services, paid out just over US$5 billion.

the U.S. announcement that it would cut such payments sparked an outcry around the world and Verma said India would present its case against the decision by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to the team from Washington.

"We have responded to the FCC and said we cannot agree to everything they have said, especially on the time frame for achieving the desired tariff level," said A.V. Gokak, chairman of India's Telecom Commission.
Without callback volume, calls from the United States to India were already about 16 times heavier than from India to the United States, Gokak said.
